reasons: Only five of the file's eight sections were provided, so the coverage gate and standing sections are not reviewed here.
Pinned counts must be updated by hand whenever the golden data changes.

terms.meaning: A test runner for front-end code.
A fixed sample of known cases that the tests use as reference data.
The smallest difference that counts as a real disagreement, to allow for rounding.
A small, gradual change in a value that could be a sign of a bug.
A test that compares constants in two languages, here TypeScript and Python, to make sure they match.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Explains why confidence is recalculated
sections.what: The header comment says the file tests the confidence calculation against the real records, and in particular the branch that fires when a stored score does not match its features.
sections.why: The comment says that a branch never run against real data is a branch nobody knows works, and that the argument for recalculating depends on it.
sections.watch_out: Tests run against the golden artifacts, so changes to that data will change what these tests see.

sections.name: everyBlock
sections.title: Lists every confidence block
sections.what: Collects every confidence block from every golden record, keeping the case id and block name beside each one.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond supplying input to the tests.
sections.watch_out: Records without a confidence section are skipped without a message.

sections.name: the constants
sections.title: Checks constants match expected values
sections.what: Checks that the coverage scale is three and the recency half-life is 540 days, and that the module no longer exports the old neutral agreement value or the old recording flag.
sections.why: The comment says the Python constants are compared in a separate test, because this test file cannot read Python.
sections.watch_out: These two numbers must also match the Python side. That comparison lives in another file.

sections.name: every stored score reproduces from its stored features
sections.title: Checks stored scores match their features
sections.what: Checks the number of confidence blocks and the number of blocks with at least two effective citations against counts cited in the code comments. It then checks that every block reproduces its stored score, and that the largest difference is far below the tolerance.
sections.why: The comment says counts quoted in prose go stale unless a test pins them.
sections.watch_out: The pinned counts must be updated on purpose whenever the golden cases change.

sections.name: the mismatch branch
sections.title: Checks mismatch detection works
sections.what: Changes a stored score slightly and checks that the derivation reports it does not reproduce, and that the derived and stored values differ. It also checks that a drift of one hundred-thousandth is caught.
sections.why: The comment says the earlier tolerance was looser and would have let a small drift pass unnoticed.
sections.watch_out: The tolerance must stay tight. A looser value would let small drift pass silently.

sections.name: the coverage gate (part 1)
sections.title: Coverage gate tests, part one
sections.what: Checks the rules that limit how much a confidence score may claim. A score with zero effective evidence must be exactly zero, gaps must be subtracted before coverage is worked out, and each record must say whether agreement was measured by reading its stored feature list rather than guessing from the citation count.
sections.why: Likely reason: an earlier version guessed agreement from the citation count, which could not see unmeasured values. These tests lock in the replacement behaviour, as the comments describe.
sections.watch_out: The shared base record must stay a valid record, or these tests will check the wrong thing.

sections.name: the coverage gate (part 2)
sections.title: Coverage gate tests, part two
sections.what: Checks that an unmeasured agreement is left out of the score rather than counted as a neutral half. It also checks that a record whose stored value and declared features disagree is flagged as an invalid record, that consistent records are not flagged, and that a record with no feature list is reported.
sections.why: The comments say an earlier fallback invented a feature list and reported a false match. These tests stop that from coming back.
sections.watch_out: Several tests look for specific words such as INVALID RECORD, so rewording those messages will break them.

sections.name: standingOf
sections.title: standingOf tests
sections.what: Checks that a citation list with at least one id counts as grounded, and that an empty or missing list counts as unsupported. The declared prerequisite state is not tested here.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The third state, declared prerequisite, has no test in this group, so a change to it would go unnoticed here.

summary: Tests that every stored confidence score in the golden data can be reproduced from its stored features, and that the code detects a score that does not match.
purpose: Makes sure the viewer's own confidence calculation is right, so it can be trusted to flag a bad stored score.
why: The header comment says the argument for recalculating scores depends on the mismatch branch, which had never run against real data. Testing it makes that branch known to work.
how: The file gathers every confidence block from the golden records. It checks the constants, checks that the block count and a related count match the numbers cited in the code comments, and checks that every block reproduces its stored score. It also checks that a changed score and a very small drift are both detected.
inputs: The generated artifacts file, the confidence module and the constants it exports.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: Counts are pinned on purpose, so adding or removing golden cases makes the count test fail. The file covers only five of the eight sections in the packet, so the remaining three have not been reviewed here.
debug: If the reproduction test fails, print the stored and recalculated values for the failing block and check its features. If the count test fails, check whether the golden data changed. If the mismatch tests fail, check the tolerance value.
